nodes.question: How does the concept of the social license to automate enhance the understanding of demand-side management (DSM)?
nodes.answer: The social license to automate highlights the conditions under which energy users might accept automation, revealing gaps between the expectations of energy actors and the actual perspectives and aspirations of users. It addresses the legitimacy, credibility, and trust required for acceptance of DSM interventions.
nodes.paragraph: No Title Available DOI: DOI not available FullTextURL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s12053-025-10304-6 Vol. : (123456789)Energy Efficiency (2025) 18:17 https://doi.org/10.1007/s12053-25-10304-6 REVIEW ARTICLE The role of gender, age, and income in demand side management acceptance: A literature review Ida Marie Henriksen Helena Str mberg Jennifer Branlat Lisa Diamond Giulia Garzon Declan Kuch Selin Yilmaz Lenart Motnikar Received: 28 January 2024 / Accepted: 10 February 2025 The Author(s) 2025 Abstract Demand-side management (DSM) pro- grams aiming to both reduce and render household consumption more flexible are becoming increasingly essential due to ongoing energy crises and the growing integration of renewable energy into energy production. The active involvement of households and energy users is crucial to fully unlock the potential of DSM programs. As this paper demonstrates, despite more than thirty years of feminist scholarly work focusing on the home as an important site of the production of gender inequal- ity, few of these insights have been taken into account by DSM designers. Additionally, we note a broader pattern concerning gaps in knowledge regarding the diverse perspectives of energy users and their domestic contexts, all of which create obstacles to successful roll- out and scalability.
